cells.tense: You're moving toward what you want with your hands open, and the wanting and the listening are the same motion.
cells.ask: Take one more thing in today, even a small one, and let it change the plan a little
cells.core:
On a good day here, you're mid-stride and something crosses your path — a person, an idea, a line in a book — and you pick it up without breaking pace. It shifts the route a little and you let it. That's what an open hand looks like when you're moving. Nothing dramatic.

What you're holding is worth feeding. The plan isn't glass and neither are you, so there's room to notice what shows up along the way and let it count. That's not drift and it's not losing focus. It's the destination getting clearer as you go, which is how it was always going to get clearer.
cells.sheetLine: You're moving and still open to what you meet on the way.
cells.verb: opening to what's here before you know what it is
cells.place: on the road you're already moving down

cells.tense: You're racing ahead to a finish line you can't see yet, bracing for how it'll come out.
cells.ask: Pick the one result you actually care about and let the rest take care of itself
cells.core:
When this is working on the road, you're moving hard and you can still hear what's coming at you. A detour shows up and you take it without a fight, because the goal is the goal and the path is negotiable. You're going somewhere and you're not white-knuckling the wheel. Both at once, and it looks easy.

Lately the pushing has closed the window. Every sign gets read as a verdict on whether you'll make it. It's not that you want too much — it's that the wanting has stopped letting anything in. Decide what you're actually after, just that one thing, and loosen the grip on the rest. Direction you chose holds better than direction you forced.

cells.tense: You're standing at a starting line you crossed a while back, still waiting for the gun.
cells.ask: Stop at the first true thing today and let it move you, even a little
cells.core:
On this road when it's going well, you feel the pull before you have a reason for it and you go anyway. Someone mentions something and your chest answers before your head does, and you follow that. That's the whole engine — feeling the next thing and letting it point the way.

The thing you want is still out there and you've gone quiet about reaching for it. You watch other people move and something flickers, and then it goes. The wanting didn't leave — you just stopped letting it arrive. Being open doesn't ask you to build a whole life in an afternoon. One moment where something lands and you don't wave it off is enough to start. The direction comes back when you let yourself feel the pull again.
cells.sheetLine: You still want it. You've stopped letting yourself feel that.

cells.tense: You're steering toward what you want and calling it just the situation, not you choosing.
cells.ask: Notice one thing you did today out of wanting it, and say that's what it was
cells.core:
On the road when this is clear, you know which turns were yours. You can point at a choice and say why, and the why starts with you. It's not a big statement. It's just that when someone asks how you got here, you don't describe the traffic — you describe the driving.

These days you're moving toward things and you talk about it like it just happens. There are choices you make every day that shape where this goes, and you file them under circumstance. The wanting is running the show while you describe yourself as going along with it. You don't need a bigger plan. Catch one moment where you picked something on purpose and name it as yours. The direction is already yours — start saying so.
cells.sheetLine: You're already choosing this. You just haven't claimed it.
